description: A procurement lead must decide how to disposition four steel coils whose receiving labels do not match the accompanying mill certificates, and must finalize their job assignments, release testing, shipment plan, and processing controls with input from quality, materials engineering, production control, and environmental health and safety.

shared_context.S1: The receiving dock is holding four steel coils, labeled C1, C2, C3, and C4, because the labels do not match the accompanying mill-certificate packet.
shared_context.S2: Each coil weighs 300 kilograms, and the coils are intended for two active production jobs.
shared_context.S3: Material release requires an identity check, a documented job assignment, and a receiving disposition before a coil can be sent to production.
shared_context.S4: At the daily receiving disposition review, Mara follows the routine of asking quality assurance, materials engineering, production control, and environmental health and safety for their status before making the binding disposition.
shared_context.S5: Each function records its status as a formal disposition fact during the review; Mara may settle once the four status facts and the related follow-up commitments are recorded, without waiting for the physical paperwork or controls to be completed after the meeting.

PF1.text: Jon's receiving inspection found that the certificate mismatch requires 100% positive-material-identification testing on all four coils before any of them can be released; he completed the inspection this morning, but the inspection worksheet is still waiting to be attached to the receiving record.

PF2.text: Priya's handheld PMI test confirmed that C1 and C2 are grade 304 stainless steel and C3 and C4 are grade 316 stainless steel; she ran the tests this morning, but the results are still in her instrument's export queue.

PF3.text: Luis's current production schedule assigns exactly 600 kilograms of grade 304 to Job Alpha for Thursday and exactly 600 kilograms of grade 316 to Job Beta for Monday; he issued the schedule revision this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the receiving disposition system.

PF4.text: Nadia's floor review found that processing the grade 316 coils requires the dedicated chromium-bearing-metal dust collector and a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary around the cutting station; she recorded the finding during today's walk-through, but the temporary-control notice has not yet been posted.

acceptance_conditions: All four coils must receive 100% positive-material-identification testing before release.
C1 and C2 must be assigned to Job Alpha, while C3 and C4 must be assigned to Job Beta.
Exactly 600 kilograms must be planned for Job Alpha on Thursday and exactly 600 kilograms for Job Beta on Monday.
The shipment plan must identify Job Alpha's Thursday shipment and Job Beta's Monday shipment.
Processing the grade 316 coils must require the dedicated chromium-bearing-metal dust collector.
Processing the grade 316 coils must require a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary.
The receiving disposition system entry must be included as a commitment.
The material-identity finding must be cited in the decision-maker's justification.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['system_entry', 'documented_job_assignment', 'job_assignment', 'receiving_disposition_recorded'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: The exact requirement for 100% PMI testing on all four coils changes the identity decision to four tested coils and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The confirmed grade mapping changes C1 and C2 to Job Alpha and C3 and C4 to Job Beta.
The exact 600-kilogram quantities and Thursday/Monday dates change both structured shipment fields, while the unentered revision requires a receiving-disposition-system commitment.
The processing finding changes the grade 316 controls to a dedicated chromium-bearing-metal dust collector and an exact 1.5-meter exclusion boundary.
